title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: High glum and high CPL brightness are often opposed: Eu(III) 5D0→7F1 can give glum > 0.1 because it is purely magnetic-dipole, but its low intensity and branching ratio limit brightness, whereas hypersensitive 5D0→7F2 is brighter but usually has a less favorable |μ|/|m| ratio.
explanation: The 5D0→7F1 probability is crystal-field independent and is used as an intensity reference, yet its magnetic-dipole character keeps the branching ratio low. 5D0→7F2 intensity grows by the forced-electric-dipole/dynamic-coupling mechanism in low-symmetry, polarizable ligand fields. The review treats the resulting glum-versus-quantum-yield tension as a general design contradiction, and later recommends reporting CPL brightness BCPL so the two quantities can be compared together.
scope: Eu(III) coordination compounds used as CPL emitters; the same trade-off is stated more generally for Ln(III) complexes.
conditions: 5D0→7F1 is the ΔJ = 1 magnetic-dipole transition; 5D0→7F2 is forced electric dipole and hypersensitive.
caveats: The explicit algebraic definition of BCPL (Eq. 14) is cited but not reproduced in the Markdown. Promising compounds with glum 0.1–1 and quantum yields above 10% show the trade-off is not absolute.
